content:
Hi everyone!

My name is Samuël Borza, and I am a Marie Curie postdoctoral fellow at the University of Vienna. I work closely with the Lorentzian Geometry group there. I specialise in sub-Riemannian, sub-Finsler, and sub-Lorentzian geometry, and I have recently developed an interest in Causal Set Theory.

I learned about Lean because a good friend of mine, James Huang (he is going to introduce himself in another post :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:), was doing a master’s at Imperial College and took the infamous Formalising Mathematics course by Kevin Buzzard.

His final project was on the formalisation of part of a direct proof of the transcendence of π\piπ. After he finished the master’s, he asked me to team up with him, and we eventually managed to finish the proof, which we have just uploaded here.

It’s our first time contributing to Lean, so apologies if we did not follow the best practices of sharing early and getting in touch from the start. We literally did not check how things are done in the community :melting_face: we did have fun!

Hope to contribute more to mathlib in the future :grinning:
